p: Build more expressive game audio with less MetaSound wiring.

AudioPhysx is an Unreal Engine C++ audio toolkit focused on sample playback, procedural acoustic behaviour, physical-material routing and Blueprint audio integration. It provides native MetaSound nodes intended to simplify common game-audio tasks while keeping the important sound-design controls exposed.

This site documents the current AudioPhysx UE5.8.4 development source, including the latest Start Loop End RPM change. The commercial release and supported-platform matrix are not yet finalized. Review compatibility before using these pages as a release guarantee.
Install AudioPhysx into your Unreal Engine project.
Explore the MetaSound node catalogue or Blueprint integrations.
Playback nodes — randomized sounds, sequences, layers and specialized players.
Acoustics nodes — material transmission, paths, impact shaping, reflections and directivity.
Propagation nodes — delay, air absorption and Doppler-inspired processing.
QoL nodes — control smoothing, trigger probability, cooldowns and routing.
Blueprint integration — world-aware playback, flyby and acoustic querying.

AudioPhysx combines physically motivated calculations with perceptual approximations. A believable game-audio result is the goal; not every node is a complete physical simulation. Each reference page explains the data or controls it expects.
New to AudioPhysx? Follow these pages in order. You can reach a first playable result without using acoustic path components or writing C++.
The documentation currently targets the AudioPhysx UE5.8.4 development source. The final Fab package may have a different verified version matrix; that will be published on Compatibility.

Unreal location/distance values in these inputs are usually centimetres unless explicitly marked (m); speed inputs may be metres per second; RPM means events per minute. The node labels specify units.
The exact installation method depends on whether you received the finished Fab code plugin or a private development source build.
Obtain the AudioPhysx plugin for a supported engine version through Fab/Epic's plugin installation flow.
Open your project and go to Edit → Plugins.
Search for AudioPhysx, enable it if needed and restart the editor when requested.
Open a MetaSound Source and search for AP: or AudioPhysx in the add-node menu.
These steps describe the intended customer workflow. The Fab distribution has not been verified here. Do not claim an engine or platform is supported until you have tested the final packaged plugin.
Close Unreal Editor and disable Live Coding.
Put the complete plugin directory (including its .uplugin descriptor) in YourProject/Plugins/AudioPhysx/.
Regenerate project files if required, and build the Editor target with the supported toolchain.
Reopen Unreal Editor and confirm the nodes appear.
Do not copy a Source ZIP by itself and expect a working plugin: a distributable code plugin also needs its descriptor and appropriate packaging metadata.
Create a new MetaSound Source and confirm you can add AP: Random Wave Player, connect a wave array and play a sample. See Your first MetaSound.
Plugin enabled, editor restarted, rebuild completed
Match engine version and platform/toolchain, check first compiler error
Old node pins or registration errors
Close editor, perform clean rebuild without stale plugin intermediates
In this walkthrough you'll make three recordings play in order using AP: Sequence Wave Player. Each sound starts once the previous sound has finished—no manual delay values.
Create a new MetaSound Source with a mono output. Open it in the MetaSound editor.
Search for AP: Sequence Wave Player in AudioPhysx → Playback. Add it to the graph.
Expand the Sequence Waves group to the number of recordings you want. Assign a Wave Asset to each Wave slot in the intended order.
Preview the MetaSound. You should hear each recording sequentially. With Loop Sequence enabled the list repeats; without looping it ends after the last valid sound.
If you're creating a long-running ambient or interactive source, don't wire On Finished in a way that stops the Source before you want it to end.
Next: Random Sequence Wave Player or Start Loop End Player.
Trigger pins describe moments: start playback, stop playback, release a held effect or announce completion.
Audio pins carry sample buffers. Out Mono produces a single audio channel.
Control pins carry values such as gain, pitch, distance, speed or material selection.

l: On Finished is not the same as Stop
p: In AudioPhysx Wave Players, natural completion usually produces On Finished; an explicit Stop often cancels without issuing that natural-completion event. Check each node page for precise behaviour.

An effect such as Early Reflections or Acoustic Paths can extend the audio tail after the source Wave Player finishes. Connect the source's completion event to the processing node's Source Finished input and use the processor's output completion where appropriate.

Some nodes allow the graph author to add more ranges, steps or waves. Change the group counts in the MetaSound editor and inspect the generated pins. For AP: Surface Wave Player, pins may additionally depend on project settings, so route edits deserve extra care.
Don't connect a Wave Player's On Finished directly to the MetaSound Source's finished trigger if other downstream effects still have audible tails.

AudioPhysx can publish acoustic parameter values from Blueprint/world systems to a MetaSound graph. Use the interfaces and names included with your installed plugin build, rather than creating independent duplicate parameters with similar names.
The current source includes a compact selected-route contract:
Float Array: [delay ms, low loss dB, mid loss dB, high loss dB]
Connect that array to AP: Acoustic Paths when using the managed route system.

Other parameters are grouped by propagation, atmosphere, transmission and impact; refer to your installed interface list in the MetaSound editor. Avoid manually mixing data from different interface versions.
When an engine or plugin interface changes, compare the generated MetaSound pins before saving modified graphs. This is particularly important for projects with previously authored material routes.

AudioPhysx provides functions and components for connecting game-world information to audio. These features operate outside the MetaSound audio-render loop.

Physical playback helpers — play sounds and register audio components.
Acoustic path queries — query path information from world geometry.
Acoustic components — emitter, barrier, portal and bridge concepts.

l: Is AudioPhysx a replacement for Unreal audio?
p: No. It extends MetaSounds and game-audio workflows. Unreal's own attenuation, concurrency, mixer, audio components and Sound Cues remain part of a typical project.

No. The flyby path helpers use supplied positions and speed; the acoustic/material tools can use Blueprint or C++ data provided by your game. Some integrations use world traces or primitive components, but not a bespoke Chaos rigid-body simulation.
No. Playback nodes output recordings; DSP nodes modify existing audio; utility nodes shape triggers/controls; Blueprint helpers connect game-world information.

l: Why is Out Mono used so often?
p: Many nodes deliberately produce mono audio to leave source spatialization and further processing to the MetaSound Source and Unreal audio pipeline.

l: Is On Finished triggered when I stop a Wave Player?
p: Not necessarily. On several players, an explicit Stop cancels playback without the natural completion event. Consult that player's reference.

l: Does changing Acoustic Physical Materials change existing recording assets?
p: No. Material parameters influence routing/evaluation or sound-selection logic. They don't destructively edit imported Wave Assets.

l: Does AudioPhysx include Sound Cue nodes?
p: Not in the development source represented by this documentation. Sound Cue quality-of-life extensions are planned and should not be advertised as included until shipped.

l: Will it work in Unreal Engine 6?
p: No future UE6 compatibility claim has been verified or promised. Check the supported engine matrix for the version you purchase.
